title: Clinical skills: history, examination and reasoning
audience: a medical student in the preclinical years
purpose: Take a complete history, communicate with empathy, perform the general, head and neck, cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, neurological, musculoskeletal and skin examinations, present patients, write notes and reason toward a differential diagnosis.

weeks.2: Communication, empathy and breaking bad news
weeks.3: Vital signs and the general survey
weeks.4: The head, eyes, ears, nose and throat examination
weeks.10: The skin and lymph node examination

blocks.deliverable: Practice an interview with the SPIKES approach.
Record and interpret a set of vital signs.
Describe heart sounds and breath sounds and what changes them.
Week 7 midterm; localize findings from a neurological examination.
Describe a skin lesion in standard terms.
Present a case in three minutes and defend a differential.
Submit the project; take an unseen 150 minute final in week 14.

project: Standardized-patient practice: run three full encounters with a partner from supplied scripts, write SOAP notes, and self-assess against the rubric.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
